drafts.title: Front end meets stated pedestrian-protection outcome (regulatory ask)
drafts.description: Customers expect the vehicle's front-end to meet the new EU pedestrian protection requirements so they feel the car is safer for pedestrians.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request is a regulatory/homologation requirement and must be validated by the official EU pedestrian protection certification tests applicable at time of launch.
assumptions: This is a regulatory certification request (EU pedestrian protection) and validation will occur through the applicable homologation/certification process.
uncertainties: Exact test protocols and pass/fail thresholds depend on the final EU regulation text and the homologation authority's procedures at launch.
drafts.scope_reason: This item is a regulation/homologation request (out of scope for product feature requirements).

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag certified to FMVSS 208 (customer request)
drafts.description: Customers want assurance that the rear-seat airbags meet FMVSS 208 certification so rear passengers get crash-protection validated to US safety standards.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request requires FMVSS 208 certification; conformance must be demonstrated by passing the FMVSS 208 test program at launch.
assumptions: FMVSS 208 certification is a regulatory/homologation process performed by accredited test labs and authorities.
uncertainties: Certification test procedures and any scope changes by authorities before launch.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification request (regulation/homologation) rather than a customer-experience feature.

drafts.title: Request for a specific rotary encoder part (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked for a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (specific component request).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a component specification request; engineering decision required to select/validate a 12-bit magnetic encoder per supplier/production constraints.
assumptions: Customers named a specific component (12-bit magnetic encoder).
uncertainties: Feasibility vs. HMI requirements, supplier availability and EMC/validation constraints.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific part/component request (engineering specification) — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for thicker laminated side glass (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the side windows use 4.5 mm laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a glass-thickness/material specification request; selection and validation of 4.5 mm laminated side glass must be completed by engineering/sourcing.
assumptions: Signal requests a specific glass thickness and construction (4.5 mm laminated).
uncertainties: Trade-offs vs. weight, NVH performance, cost and glass supplier capabilities.

drafts.title: Business request for a 5‑year residual value guarantee (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers request BMW guarantee a 60% residual value after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a commercial/financial commitment request and must be decided by BMW finance/marketing; not a product engineering requirement.
assumptions: This request is a business guarantee rather than a vehicle feature.
uncertainties: Feasibility depends on corporate financing strategy and market conditions at time of launch.
drafts.scope_reason: Commercial/financial request (out of scope for product requirements).

drafts.title: Request to reduce production cost per car by 8% (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked BMW to cut production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an internal production/cost target for BMW and not a direct customer-facing vehicle requirement.
assumptions: Signal requests a corporate cost target rather than a customer experience change.
uncertainties: Implementation depends on supplier negotiations, design-to-cost activities and production strategies.
drafts.scope_reason: Corporate cost target (out of scope for product feature requirements).

drafts.title: Front seats provide longer, adjustable thigh support for tall drivers
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend front-seat cushion depth so the seat supports more of their thigh without feeling like they are sliding off the edge.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front-seat cushion must provide an adjustable thigh-support extension of at least 60 mm beyond the baseline cushion depth; extension measured from the forward edge of the standard cushion must be ≥ 60 mm and usable at the full range of seat positions.
assumptions: 60 mm is a realistic and perceptible improvement for tall drivers based on current seat architecture.
Mechanism can be packaged without reducing other seat adjustment ranges.
uncertainties: Exact required extension for the 95th-percentile tall user may vary by body proportions.
Integration impact on seat heating/airbag/weight is to be validated.

drafts.title: Cup holders fit common bottles and hold them securely
drafts.description: Customers can place common water bottles and travel mugs into the cup holders and drive without the bottle tipping or rattling.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders must accept cylindrical containers up to 90 mm diameter and 300 mm height and retain them without tipping during a lateral acceleration of 0.5 g in laboratory testing.
assumptions: 90 mm diameter covers the majority of large consumer bottles and travel tumblers in the market.
uncertainties: Very wide sport containers (>90 mm) will not be covered; adapters or configurable inserts may be needed.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on first attempt across real-world conditions
drafts.description: Customers can open the hands-free tailgate with a single successful foot/gesture without repeated attempts during normal use (including typical clothing and footwear).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Tailgate must open on the first valid hands-free gesture in ≥ 90% of attempts over 200 consecutive trials across representative conditions (ambient temperatures from -10°C to +40°C, with typical footwear and with light trunk loads), and the opening action must start within 2.5 seconds of the detected gesture.
assumptions: Representative conditions include common shoe types, light mud/dirt on sensors and moderate trunk loading.
Detection zone and user instructions are clearly communicated to customers.
uncertainties: Performance under heavy contamination (deep mud/ice) or when user stands outside the detection zone.
Edge-case footwear (very soft/very narrow shoes) may affect detection rate.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with expanded color and brightness options and saved presets
drafts.description: Customers can choose from a wide range of ambient-light colors and fine-grained brightness levels and save personalized lighting presets per user profile.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Interior ambient lighting shall offer at least 64 distinct color choices, at least 10 discrete brightness levels, and allow customers to save a minimum of 4 custom color/brightness presets per user profile.
assumptions: LED lighting hardware and software can support 64 selectable colors and 10 brightness steps without creating glare or driver distraction.
uncertainties: Perception of color differences may vary by interior trim and material reflectance.
Regulatory limits on certain colors for driver displays may require gating some options while vehicle is in motion.

drafts.title: Memory seats restore saved positions reliably (high success rate)
drafts.description: When a customer selects a saved seat profile, the seat moves to the stored position consistently so the driver does not need to adjust manually after selecting memory.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Selecting a saved memory profile must position the seat within ±10 mm linearly and ±2° rotationally of stored values and succeed on the first restore attempt in at least 98% of 100 repeated cycles under normal vehicle power conditions.
assumptions: Measurement method for position tolerance is consistent (same reference points used for storage and verification).
Normal vehicle power means nominal 12V system without low-voltage/degraded conditions.
uncertainties: Failure modes may be due to mechanical binding, sensor drift, or software profile mismatch; root cause will determine fix scope.

drafts.title: Exterior door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Customers expect flush door handles to open on first attempt in winter conditions and not be blocked by common ice/frost situations.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Door handles must operate (open) on the first attempt in ≥ 95% of cycles after exposure to an ice/frost chamber test with up to 5 mm surface ice accumulation at -15°C and when tested with common door seals in place.
assumptions: Test replicates typical freezing/ice formation on exterior door areas; -15°C and 5 mm ice represent severe but common winter conditions.
uncertainties: Extreme conditions (below -30°C) or unusual ice types (thick glaze from freezing rain) may still affect operation.
Mitigations may include heating, drain paths or manual release instructions which can affect cost and packaging.

drafts.title: Rear legroom at least as generous as main competitors
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers should experience legroom that is no smaller than the main competitors in the segment so rear-seat comfort is competitive.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measure rear knee clearance (distance from back of front seat to knee reference on a standardized 95th-percentile passenger) and demonstrate interior space ≥ 970 mm; the measurement method and competitor baseline must be documented.
assumptions: 970 mm is a realistic target representing 'at least as good as main competitors' based on current market competitor dimensions; competitor data will be collected and validated before final acceptance.
Measurement uses a standardized anthropometric rig and defined front-seat position (e.g., driver-seat set to its average position for the competitor comparison).
uncertainties: Competitor dimensions may change; final benchmark set must be locked prior to final validation.
Packaging trade-offs (battery, HVAC, chassis) may limit available rear legroom improvements.
